comment:
* A color appearance model, based on CAM16, extended to use L* as the lightness dimension, and
 * coupled to a gamut mapping algorithm. Creates a color system, enables a digital design system.

variables.name: DL_MAX
variables.comment: The maximum difference between the requested L* and the L* returned.

variables.name: DE_MAX
variables.comment: The maximum color distance, in CAM16-UCS, between a requested color and the color returned.

variables.name: LIGHTNESS_SEARCH_ENDPOINT
variables.comment: is less than this, the binary search terminates.

variables.name: mHue
variables.comment: CAM16 color dimensions, see getters for documentation.

variables.name: mJstar
variables.comment: Coordinates in UCS space. Used to determine color distance, like delta E equations in L*a*b*.

methods.name: float getHue()
methods.comment: Hue in CAM16

methods.name: float getChroma()
methods.comment: Chroma in CAM16

methods.name: float getJ()
methods.comment: Lightness in CAM16

methods.name: float getQ()
methods.comment:
* Brightness in CAM16. * *

Prefer lightness, brightness is an absolute quantity. For example, a sheet of white paper * is much brighter viewed in sunlight than in indoor light, but it is the lightest object under * any lighting.

methods.name: float getM()
methods.comment:
* Colorfulness in CAM16. * *

Prefer chroma, colorfulness is an absolute quantity. For example, a yellow toy car is much * more colorful outside than inside, but it has the same chroma in both environments.

methods.name: float getS()
methods.comment:
* Saturation in CAM16. * *

Colorfulness in proportion to brightness. Prefer chroma, saturation measures colorfulness * relative to the color's own brightness, where chroma is colorfulness relative to white.

methods.name: float getJStar()
methods.comment: Lightness coordinate in CAM16-UCS

methods.name: float getAStar()
methods.comment: a* coordinate in CAM16-UCS

methods.name: float getBStar()
methods.comment: b* coordinate in CAM16-UCS

methods.name: public static int toColor(@FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 360.0) float hue, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, toInclusive = false) float chroma, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 100.0) float lStar)
methods.comment:
* Given a hue & chroma in CAM16, L* in L*a*b*, return an ARGB integer. The chroma of the color
     * returned may, and frequently will, be lower than requested. Assumes the color is viewed in
     * the default ViewingConditions.

methods.name: static CamColor fromColor(@ColorInt int color)
methods.comment:
* Create a color appearance model from a ARGB integer representing a color. It is assumed the
     * color was viewed in the default ViewingConditions.
     *
     * The alpha component is ignored, CamColor only represents opaque colors.

methods.name: public static void getM3HCTfromColor(@ColorInt int color, @Size(3) float @NonNull [] outM3HCT)
methods.comment:
* * Get the values for M3HCT color from ARGB color. * * HCT color space is a new color space proposed in Material Design 3 * @see * About Color Spaces * *
    *
  • outM3HCT[0] is Hue in M3HCT [0, 360); invalid values are corrected.
    • *
  • outM3HCT[1] is Chroma in M3HCT [0, ?); Chroma may decrease because chroma has a *different maximum for any given hue and tone.
    • *
  • outM3HCT[2] is Tone in M3HCT [0, 100]; invalid values are corrected.
    • *
* *@param color is the ARGB color value we use to get its respective M3HCT values. *@param outM3HCT 3-element array which holds the resulting M3HCT components (Hue, * Chroma, Tone).

methods.name: static void fromColorInViewingConditions(@ColorInt int color, @NonNull ViewingConditions viewingConditions, @Size(7) float @Nullable [] outCamColor, @Size(3) float @NonNull [] outM3HCT)
methods.comment:
* Create a color appearance model from a ARGB integer representing a color, specifying the
     * ViewingConditions in which the color was viewed. Prefer Cam.fromColor.

methods.name: private static CamColor fromJch(@FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 100.0) float j, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, toInclusive = false) float c, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 360.0) float h)
methods.comment:
* Create a CAM from lightness, chroma, and hue coordinates. It is assumed those coordinates
     * were measured in the default ViewingConditions.

methods.name: private static CamColor fromJchInFrame(@FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 100.0) float j, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, toInclusive = false) float c, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 360.0) float h, ViewingConditions viewingConditions)
methods.comment:
* Create a CAM from lightness, chroma, and hue coordinates, and also specify the
     * ViewingConditions where the color was seen.

methods.name: float distance(@NonNull CamColor other)
methods.comment:
* Distance in CAM16-UCS space between two colors. * *

Much like L*a*b* was designed to measure distance between colors, the CAM16 standard * defined a color space called CAM16-UCS to measure distance between CAM16 colors.

methods.name: int viewedInSrgb()
methods.comment: Returns perceived color as an ARGB integer, as viewed in default ViewingConditions.

methods.name: int viewed(@NonNull ViewingConditions viewingConditions)
methods.comment: Returns color perceived in a ViewingConditions as an ARGB integer.

methods.name: static int toColor(@FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 360.0) float hue, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, toInclusive = false) float chroma, @FloatRange(from = 0.0, to = 100.0) float lstar, @NonNull ViewingConditions viewingConditions)
methods.comment:
* Given a hue & chroma in CAM16, L* in L*a*b*, and the ViewingConditions in which the * color will be viewed, return an ARGB integer. * *

The chroma of the color returned may, and frequently will, be lower than requested. This * is a fundamental property of color that cannot be worked around by engineering. For example, * a red hue, with high chroma, and high L* does not exist: red hues have a maximum chroma * below 10 in light shades, creating pink.

methods.comment: Returns null if no J could be found that generated a color with L* `lstar`.
